prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses reflects our internal calculation and judgment of the appropriate amount of the allowance for credit losses. We maintain the allowance for credit losses at levels we believe are appropriate to cover our estimate of expected credit losses over the life of loans in the portfolio as of the end of the reporting period. The allowance for credit losses is determined through detailed quarterly analyses of our loan portfolio. The allowance for credit losses is based on our loss experience, changes in the economic environment, reasonable and supportable forecasts, as well as an ongoing assessment of credit quality and environmental factors not reflected in historical loss rates. Additional qualitative factors that are considered in determining the amount of the allowance for credit losses are c oncentrations of credit risk (geographic, large borrower, and industry), changes in underwriting standards, changes in collateral value, experience and depth of lending staff, trends in delinquencies, and the volume and terms of loans.

We recorded a recovery for credit losses of $72,000 during the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to a recovery for credit losses of $543,000 recorded during the three months ended September 30, 2025.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text: Noninterest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $20.0 million compared to $14.7 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $5.4 million, or 36.6%.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased $4.0 million, or 17.8%, to $26.2 million compared to interest expense of $22.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, primarily due to a $562.8 million increase in average interest-bearing deposit balances, offset by a $49.6 million decrease in the average borrowings

net.text: We recorded net income of $24.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to $17.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $7.0 million, or 40.7%. This increase was due to an $11.8 million increase in net interest income, and a $2.9 million decrease in income taxes, offset by a $5.4 million increase in noninterest expense, a $471,000 reduction in credit-loss recovery and a $1.8 million decrease in noninterest income.

Net interest income.text: Net interest margin and net interest income are influenced by internal and external factors. Internal factors include balance sheet changes on both volume and mix and pricing decisions, and external factors include changes in market interest rates, competition, and the shape of the interest rate yield curve. The year-over-year increase in our net interest margin is primarily driven by higher yields on average interest-earning assets and lowere costs of average interest-bearing liablilities.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $4.4 million, a decrease of $1.8 million, or 29.0%, compared to $6.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Noninterest income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $16.5 million, a decrease of $871,000, or 5.0%, compared to $17.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

intro.text: MetroCity Bankshares, Inc. (the “Company”), a bank holding company incorporated in 2014 and headquartered in the Atlanta metropolitan area. We primarily operate through our wholly-owned banking subsidiary, Metro City Bank, a Georgia state-chartered commercial bank that was founded in 2006 (the “Bank”). We currently operate 29 full-service branch locations in multi-ethnic communities in Alabama, California, Florida, Georgia, New York, New Jersey, Texas and Virginia. As of December 31, 2025, we had total assets of $4.77 billion, total loans held for investment of $4.08 billion, total deposits of $3.65 billion and total shareholders’ equity of $544.2 million.
